class_list_fixed.definition: The name states a quantity, locus, component or relation that the Data Dictionary source text contradicts.

The source text states a qualifier of the quantity — a counting basis, a species basis, a weighting or average, a normalisation, a coordinate convention, a component or a locus — and the name leaves it out.
The stored definition (description or documentation) contradicts the Data Dictionary source text.
The stored name and the stored definition describe different quantities or different scopes, even if each is internally consistent.
The stored unit does not fit the quantity the name states: it is dimensionally wrong for that kind of quantity, or it is the wrong unit for the stated kind of quantity.
The assigned physics domain is not the domain of the quantity the source describes.
The name denotes the same quantity as another live standard name listed for it, so the catalog carries one quantity twice.

A.rationale: The name specifies 'measurement position', contradicting sources for actuator and hardware locations such as NBI beamlets (nbi/unit/beamlets_group/beamlets/positions/z) and polarizer centre (ece/polarizer/centre/z). Furthermore, the assigned physics domain 'equilibrium' does not fit these diagnostic and heating/actuator coordinates.

B.rationale: The sources' "Vertical (Z) coordinate of position" and unit "m" match the name and definition. However, the positions occur predominantly in diagnostic or device structures such as "reflectometer_fluctuation", "bolometer", "nbi" and "langmuir_probes"; this generic measurement-position coordinate is not specifically an equilibrium quantity, so the assigned domain "equilibrium" is wrong.

C.rationale: 'delta position suprathermal' describes a displacement, not the named position coordinate; 'position average' supplies an omitted averaging qualifier. The definition instead specifies a 'position vector from the coordinate origin' and excludes 'aggregating coordinates over a population'. Sources including 'nbi/unit/beamlets_group/beamlets/positions/z' describe cross-device geometry, not an equilibrium-specific quantity.

A.rationale: Source 3 states the quantity represents electron pressure in the 'post-crash core plasma state', but the stored definition states it is 'in the plasma edge and scrape-off layer'. This contradicts the source text and introduces a disagreement between the locus specified in the name and the locus in the definition.

B.rationale: Source 3 places the named post-crash pressure "in the post-crash core plasma state"; the stored description instead puts it "in the plasma edge and scrape-off layer", contradicting the source and assigning the name a different spatial scope.

C.rationale: Source 3 specifies the “post-crash core plasma state”; the stored description instead locates the pressure “in the plasma edge and scrape-off layer.” This contradicts the source and gives the named post-sawtooth-crash quantity an incompatible edge/SOL scope.

A.rationale: The source specifies `ic_antennas/antenna/module/strap/outline/phi` as "Toroidal angle (φ) coordinate of outline" within the enclosing structure `strap/outline` ("Strap outline"). The standard name leaves out the locus or component qualifier `outline`, identifying the angle as belonging to the antenna strap rather than its outline.

B.rationale: The source path ends “strap/outline/phi” and states “Toroidal angle (φ) coordinate of outline,” with enclosing structure “Strap outline.” The name “toroidal_angle_of_antenna_strap” omits this outline-point locus, although the stored definition explicitly supplies it.

C.rationale: The source specifies “Toroidal angle (φ) coordinate of outline” under “Strap outline”; the definition specifies “each antenna-strap outline point.” The name “toroidal_angle_of_antenna_strap” omits the outline-point locus and is broader in scope than the stored per-point definition.

A.rationale: The definition states that this quantity 'is the envelope phase, not the carrier oscillation phase.' This contradicts Source 1 ('Phase (φ) measured for a specific interferometer wavelength channel') and Source 2 ('Measured phase of the probing wave relative to its launch phase'), where the measured quantity is the carrier wave phase.

B.rationale: The name leaves out stated qualifiers: Source 1 requires “Phase … for a specific interferometer wavelength channel, corrected for fringe jumps”; Source 2 requires phase “relative to its launch phase”; Source 3 specifies the “envelope” phase “measured relative to the launch phase.”

C.rationale: Sources specify phase “corrected from fringe jumps,” “relative to the phase at launch,” and “of the envelope of the probing signal.” The name “wave_phase_of_wave_beam” omits the fringe-jump correction, launch reference, and envelope qualifier.

A.rationale: The standard name, definition, unit, and physics domain consistently describe the vertical coordinate (Z) of a divertor strike point, matching the Data Dictionary sources in both equilibrium constraints and summary boundary parameters.

B.rationale: The sources and stored definition share one quantity: the vertical Z coordinate, in metres, of an individual divertor strike point. Source 1’s measured strike-point array and sources 2–3’s outer/inner points fit the definition’s “one selected strike point, including separately identified inner and outer strike points”; no conflicting scope, unit, or domain is stated.

C.rationale: The shared quantity is the vertical (Z) coordinate of an individual divertor strike point. The source states “Array of strike points, for each of them the RZ position is given”; the definition states “Vertical coordinate of a selected divertor strike point.” Inner and outer entries identify particular strike points.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition consistently specify the vertical (Z) coordinate of the measurement position for an electron cyclotron emission (ECE) diagnostic channel.

B.rationale: The source 'Vertical (Z) coordinate of position' under 'Position of the measurements' and 'ece/channel' denotes an ECE channel’s measurement height; the definition likewise gives the 'Signed vertical coordinate ... measurement position', with matching unit m and ECE diagnostics domain.

C.rationale: The source’s “Vertical (Z) coordinate of position,” enclosed by “Position of the measurements” under ece/channel, is the named and defined vertical coordinate of an ECE channel’s measurement position. The unit m is appropriate.

A.rationale: The sources, name, and definition describe the detected photoelectron or photon rate (s^-1) per spectral channel or wavelength pixel of a spectrometer channel, with electronic gain compensation and relative calibration applied.

B.rationale: The name’s “spectral_rate” omits the stated counting basis and pixel locus: “photoelectrons per unit time per wavelength pixel.” The definition also conflicts with Source 2: it specifies “photoelectrons” and applies “to each wavelength pixel,” whereas Source 2 states “Detected photon count rate” and “number of photons per unit time recorded by the detector.”

C.rationale: The stored definition specifies “Detected photoelectron rate assigned to each wavelength pixel.” Source 2 instead specifies “Detected photon count rate” and “number of photons per unit time recorded by the detector.” Photon counts and photoelectron counts are distinct counting bases; the stored definition does not represent Source 2.

A.rationale: Major radius (radial coordinate) of a magnetic flux surface at its inboard midplane intersection.

B.rationale: The source states "Major radius (R) of the flux surface at the inboard (high-field side) midplane intersection"; the name and stored definition identify that same locus-specific major-radius coordinate. The source unit "m" fits, and the enclosing equilibrium profile structure supports the assigned equilibrium domain.

C.rationale: The source states “Major radius (R) of the flux surface at the inboard (high-field side) midplane intersection,” matching the name and stored definition’s “Major-radius coordinate of a magnetic flux surface at its inboard midplane intersection.” The unit m and equilibrium domain are appropriate.

A.rationale: The source specifies 'apparent_temperature' ('apparent surface temperature from an infrared camera frame'), whereas the name omits the qualifier 'apparent' and the definition contradicts the source by defining it as 'thermodynamic temperature'.

B.rationale: Source: “Processed 2D image of apparent surface temperature”. The name omits “apparent”; the definition instead specifies “thermodynamic temperature” and a “local scalar” at a surface point, contradicting the source’s apparent-temperature 2D image.

C.rationale: The source specifies “apparent surface temperature” and “Processed image in apparent temperature.” The name omits “apparent,” while the stored definition instead asserts “thermodynamic temperature” representing the “surface material state,” which is not necessarily the apparent temperature inferred from infrared radiance.

A.rationale: Surface area of a diagnostic aperture opening.

B.rationale: The stored scope is “the diagnostic aperture opening” and “distinct from … surface_area_of_detector.” The sources instead include “Surface specification of detector,” “Surface specification of antenna emission,” and reflector documentation “Surface of the object.” Thus the aperture-only name and definition contradict source loci beyond apertures.

C.rationale: Sources specify “Surface specification of detector” and “Surface specification of reflector,” contradicting the aperture-only name and definition, “Area of the diagnostic aperture opening in its own plane.” The source “nbi/unit/aperture/surface” also describes a neutral-beam-injection aperture, not a diagnostic aperture; its domain is not “radiation_measurement_diagnostics”.

A.rationale: The source, stored name, and definitions all specify the minimum safety factor (q value) across the plasma equilibrium.

B.rationale: The source leaf 'q_min/value' is documented as 'Minimum q value' with unit '1'; its parent separately describes 'Minimum q value and position.' The name and stored definition identify the extremal safety-factor value, not its location, and the dimensionless unit and equilibrium domain fit.

C.rationale: The source specifies “Minimum q value,” matching minimum_safety_factor. The stored documentation instead selects the surface “where the magnitude of the safety factor is smallest.” The signed q at minimum |q| is not generally the minimum q, particularly when q is negative.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition consistently describe the net RF power launched into the vacuum vessel by a lower-hybrid antenna, module, or overall antenna system, with unit W in the auxiliary_heating domain.

B.rationale: The shared quantity is net lower-hybrid launched power: Source 4 says “Net RF power launched from a lower hybrid (LH) antenna into the vacuum vessel,” while Source 7 specifies “the forward power minus the reflected power.” Source 5 covers the system sum. The stored definitions agree; W and auxiliary_heating are appropriate.

C.rationale: Source 6 specifies “net RF power absorbed by the plasma.” The name specifies launched power, and the documentation defines “net power delivered across the launching aperture into the vessel.” Plasma-absorbed power and power entering the vessel are distinct quantities, so both the name and stored definition conflict with Source 6.

A.rationale: Sources 1–19 and the definition specify the field evaluated "at the reference major radius R0". The name leaves out this locus (name_omits_source). Consequently, the name denotes a spatially distributed field while the definition describes only the single-point scalar at the reference radius (name_definition_disagree).

B.rationale: Sources 1–19 specify “at the reference major radius R0”, a locus absent from the name. Source 20 instead says “on GGD grid subsets” and “given on various grid subsets”, contradicting the stored definition’s “at the reference major radius” and documentation’s “component evaluated at the reference radius”.

C.rationale: The definition specifies "at the reference major radius", but source 20 describes a "full 3D vacuum field map" and a toroidal component "given on various grid subsets", not solely R0. The unrestricted name "toroidal_vacuum_magnetic_field" also has broader spatial scope than the stored definition.

A.rationale: Polarization ellipticity is defined as the signed minor-to-major semiaxis ratio of the electric-field polarization ellipse, which is a dimensionless ratio. The stored unit 'm' (meters) is dimensionally wrong for an ellipticity.

B.rationale: The definition calls ellipticity “the signed minor-to-major semiaxis ratio,” a dimensionless quantity, yet the stored unit is “m.” The source’s “Initial ellipticity … before entering the plasma” otherwise agrees with the name and stored definition.

C.rationale: Source 2 states “Initial polarization vector,” but the name specifies ellipticity and stored documentation explicitly says “It is not the full initial polarization vector.” Both agree with Source 1, but contradict Source 2. The defined “signed minor-to-major semiaxis ratio” is dimensionless, so stored unit “m” is wrong.

A.rationale: The source path pf_passive/loop/element/turns_with_sign and description state the locus as a "passive conductor loop element" ("Each loop is comprised of a number of cross-section elements described individually"), but the standard name omits the element locus, naming only the passive loop.

B.rationale: The source leaf `pf_passive/loop/element/turns_with_sign` states: “Number of effective turns (with sign) in a passive conductor loop element.” The name omits both the signed basis and the element locus; the enclosing source says loop cross-section elements are “described individually.”

C.rationale: The source specifies "effective turns (with sign) in a passive conductor loop element"; its enclosure states "Each loop is comprised of a number of cross-section elements described individually." The name omits the signed, per-element basis and the stated convention: "positive means current is counter-clockwise when seen from above."

A.rationale: The sources, standard name, and stored definition all describe the Faraday rotation angle induced by passage of a probing beam through magnetized plasma, measured in radians.

B.rationale: Source 2: “Faraday rotation angle induced by passage of the probing beam through the magnetized plasma,” sensitive to “∫n_e·B∥ dl”; the stored definition gives the same accumulated signed rotation. The documentation treats measured and reconstructed values as realizations of one angle. Unit rad and the equilibrium-constraint domain match the sources.

C.rationale: The name and definition identify the “Faraday rotation angle induced by passage of the probing beam through the magnetized plasma.” The sources’ “Measured value” and “Value calculated from the reconstructed equilibrium” represent this same angle. The unit rad and equilibrium-constraint domain are consistent.

A.rationale: The source specifies the total is "expressed in equivalent electrons", a counting basis omitted by the name. Consequently, the stored name describes a particle or gas count (accumulated_total_gas_count), whereas the stored definition defines an equivalent-electron inventory ($N_{\mathrm{eq}} = \sum z_s N_s$), causing name and definition to disagree on the quantity.

B.rationale: The enclosing source states “Accumulated gas injected since plasma breakdown” and a total “expressed in equivalent electrons.” The name accumulated_total_gas_count omits the injection locus, post-breakdown phase, and equivalent-electron counting basis. The stored definition and unit 1 otherwise match the cumulative, species-summed quantity.

C.rationale: “accumulated_total_gas_count” names a gas count, but the definition specifies a “Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory.” Documentation defines it as “N_eq(t) = sum_s z_s N_s(t),” weighting gas particles by their equivalent-electron contributions rather than counting the gas particles themselves.

A.rationale: The standard name, definition, unit (eV), and domain describe the upper-bound photon energy of a detector channel or emissivity energy band, matching the Data Dictionary sources.

B.rationale: The sources share one quantity: "Upper photon energy bound" of a hard- or soft-X-ray energy band, in eV. The stored definition matches it as the "Upper-bound photon energy" giving the "high-energy cutoff" of an X-ray emission or detection band.

C.rationale: The shared quantity is the upper photon-energy boundary of an X-ray energy band. The sources state “Upper bound of the energy band”; the definition states “maximum energy included in an X-ray emission or detection band.” The unit eV and radiation-measurement domain fit this quantity.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition describe the vertical full height of the rectangular cross-section of a poloidal field coil or element in metres.

B.rationale: The sources state “Vertical full height of the rectangular cross-section”; the definition’s “full vertical extent of the rectangular conductor cross-section of an individual active coil element” describes that same coil-element height. The unit m fits, and magnetic_field_systems is the appropriate domain.

C.rationale: The shared quantity is the “Vertical full height” of a PF coil element’s rectangular conductor cross-section. The stored definition calls this the “nonnegative full vertical extent,” and the enclosing rectangle structure specifies “Rectangular description of the element.” The unit m and magnetic_field_systems domain fit.

A.rationale: Conversion factor from interferometric phase to line-integrated electron density for an optical line of sight at a given probing wavelength.

B.rationale: The source’s “Conversion factor from measured interferometric phase to line-integrated electron density (∫ne·dl) for a given wavelength channel” matches the stored wavelength-specific phase-to-electron-column-density coefficient along a line of sight; the unit and interferometric diagnostic domain also fit.

C.rationale: The shared quantity is the wavelength-specific phase-to-electron-column calibration factor: “Conversion factor from measured interferometric phase to line-integrated electron density” for “a given wavelength channel.” The enclosing channels are “lines-of-sight,” matching the name’s locus. The stored definition and m^-2.rad^-1 unit agree with this conversion.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition describe the elongation (kappa) of a magnetic flux surface, defined as the ratio of its vertical to radial extent.

B.rationale: Both sources describe flux-surface “Elongation (κ)” as the “ratio of the vertical to horizontal semi-axes.” The stored extent formula gives that ratio for an elliptical cross-section and defines the same vertical-to-horizontal shape measure per surface. It is dimensionless (unit 1), and the equilibrium profile source supports the assigned domain.

C.rationale: The shared quantity is flux-surface elongation: the source’s “ratio of the vertical to horizontal semi-axis of each flux surface” matches the stored “ratio of its poloidal cross-section’s vertical extent to its radial extent.” Unit “1” and domain “equilibrium” fit this dimensionless shape ratio.

A.rationale: The assigned physics domain is equilibrium, but the sources describe the geometry of hardware components such as "Array of active poloidal field (PF) coils including the central solenoid and shaping coils" (pf_active/coil) and "ic_antennas/antenna/module/strap", which belong to the magnets or heating domains rather than plasma equilibrium.

B.rationale: The source documentation states “Geometric centre R”, but the name only gives a “radial_coordinate_of_conductor_cross_section”; it omits the geometric-centre reference locus. The stored description supplies that locus and otherwise agrees with the source.

C.rationale: The name identifies a 'conductor_cross_section' generally, while documentation restricts it to 'cross-sections represented as rectangles' and 'the center position'. The sources concern 'Active PF coils', antenna straps and passive-loop geometry: conductor geometry, not an equilibrium quantity.

A.rationale: Minor radius of the plasma boundary, defined as half the difference between the maximum and minimum major radii of the boundary contour.

B.rationale: The source and stored definition agree on one quantity: “Minor radius (a) of the plasma boundary, defined as (R_max − R_min)/2 of the boundary contour,” matching “half the difference between the maximum and minimum major radii.” The plasma-boundary/LCFS locus, unit m, and equilibrium domain are consistent.

C.rationale: The source’s “Minor radius (a) of the plasma boundary, defined as (R_max − R_min)/2 of the boundary contour” matches the name and stored definition’s “half the difference between the maximum and minimum major radii.” All describe the same boundary-wide geometric minor radius; unit “m” and domain “equilibrium” fit.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition describe the minimum of the magnetic field magnitude across a magnetic flux surface.

B.rationale: Source: “Minimum magnetic field modulus (|B|_min) on each flux surface as a 1D radial profile in the MHD equilibrium.” The name and definition identify the pointwise minimum of total |B| over a flux surface; the stored unit T and equilibrium domain also match.

C.rationale: The source’s “Minimum magnetic field modulus (|B|_min) on each flux surface” matches the name and stored “Smallest total magnetic-field strength attained along a specified nested magnetic flux surface.” All describe the minimum of |B| over one flux surface. The unit T and equilibrium domain are appropriate.

A.rationale: Total additional external heating power coupled to the plasma, summing all auxiliary heating systems excluding Ohmic power.

B.rationale: Source: “Total additional external heating power coupled to the plasma, summing all auxiliary heating systems (NBI, EC, IC, and LH) excluding Ohmic power.” The name, stored definition, W unit, and auxiliary_heating domain all describe this same whole-plasma aggregate.

C.rationale: The shared quantity is “Total additional external heating power coupled to the plasma, summing all auxiliary heating systems (NBI, EC, IC, and LH) excluding Ohmic power.” The stored definition agrees; W and auxiliary_heating are appropriate.

A.rationale: The definition states that the quantity is the "measured, signed vertical-field integral" and documentation specifies "that loop's measured value", which directly contradicts Source 1 (`equilibrium/time_slice/constraints/flux_loop/reconstructed`), defined as "Value calculated from the reconstructed equilibrium".

B.rationale: The description calls this “the measured, signed vertical-field integral,” and the documentation says “that loop's measured value”; Source 1 instead states “Reconstructed value of flux loop” and “Value calculated from the reconstructed equilibrium.” The name itself is provenance-neutral, and Wb matches the stated flux.

C.rationale: Source 1 says “Reconstructed value of flux loop” and “Value calculated from the reconstructed equilibrium.” The description instead specifies “the measured, signed vertical-field integral,” and documentation specifies “that loop's measured value.” This measured-only scope contradicts Source 1 and narrows the name’s unrestricted loop-specific poloidal flux.

A.rationale: The name is general, but the stored definition restricts scope to "during a disruption" (name_definition_disagree), contradicting Source 1's "primary intrinsic heating channel in tokamak operation" (definition_contradicts_source). Additionally, "total_power" in the name contradicts Source 2, which specifies power dissipated strictly in the "halo region" (name_contradicts_source).

B.rationale: The name omits the source locus “in the plasma.” Source 2 instead states “Ohmic power dissipated in the halo region”, but the documentation integrates over “the full plasma volume” and says this is “rather than denoting only the halo-region contribution”, directly contradicting that source.

C.rationale: Source 2 specifies 'Ohmic power dissipated in the halo region' from 'halo currents'; documentation instead specifies 'the full plasma volume', explicitly 'rather than denoting only the halo-region contribution'. The unqualified 'total_power_due_to_ohmic_dissipation' also has broader scope than the definition’s 'in the plasma during a disruption'.

A.rationale: Derivative of the volume enclosed by a flux surface with respect to poloidal flux coordinate (dV/dψ).

B.rationale: Source: “Radial derivative of the volume enclosed by a flux surface with respect to poloidal flux (dV/dψ).” The name and definition state this same enclosed-volume derivative; “Wb^-1.m^3” fits m³ per Wb, and the source path places it in equilibrium.

C.rationale: The source states “Radial derivative of the volume enclosed by a flux surface with respect to poloidal flux (dV/dψ).” The name and stored definition identify this same geometric derivative. The unit Wb^-1.m^3 and equilibrium domain are appropriate.

A.rationale: The sources describe the mass flow rate of fluid or coolant passing through a balance-of-plant port, calorimetry component, or cooling loop. The name, definition, kg.s^-1 unit, and assigned physics domain accurately capture this shared quantity without contradiction or omission.

B.rationale: The sources share coolant/fluid mass throughput per unit time: “Mass flow rate (ṁ) of coolant passing through a calorimetry component”, through a cooling loop, or fluid “at a component port”. The stored dm_pass/dt definition matches, and kg.s^-1 and mechanical_measurement_diagnostics fit.

C.rationale: The shared quantity is coolant mass flow rate: “Mass flow of the coolant going through the component” and “Mass flow of the coolant going through the loop”. The port source describes fluid throughput in circuits including “e.g. divertor cooling loop”. The definition’s “mass of coolant … per unit time” and unit “kg.s^-1” agree.

A.rationale: The name, definition, and sources consistently describe the electron temperature evaluated at the magnetic axis, measured in electronvolts within the transport domain.

B.rationale: Both sources state "Electron temperature (Te) at the magnetic axis"; the stored name and definition describe that same local electron kinetic temperature, and the eV unit matches both source units.

C.rationale: Both sources state “Electron temperature (Te) at the magnetic axis,” matching the name and stored definition’s “Temperature of electrons at the magnetic axis.” The quantity is local electron temperature, appropriately expressed in eV.

A.rationale: Spectral bremsstrahlung photon radiance represents calibrated continuum spectral radiance per unit wavelength, with unit m^-3.s^-1.sr^-1 representing photons per area, second, solid angle, and wavelength.

B.rationale: The shared quantity is continuum bremsstrahlung spectral photon radiance per unit wavelength: source 2 calls it "continuum spectral radiance measured at the centre" "per unit wavelength." The stored photon-rate definition, central-wavelength evaluation, and m^-3.s^-1.sr^-1 unit consistently describe that quantity.

C.rationale: Source 2 specifies “measured at the centre of the charge exchange spectrum,” and the stored definition says “evaluated at the spectrum center.” The name “spectral_bremsstrahlung_photon_radiance” omits this spectral-location restriction and describes a broader scope than the stored definition.

A.rationale: Toroidal angle of the projection of a toroidal field (B_φ) probe's normal vector onto the horizontal plane, measured counter-clockwise from the outward major radius direction.

B.rationale: Source and stored definition both describe “the projection of a toroidal field (B_φ) probe's normal vector onto the horizontal plane,” measured from outward R, with values “modulo pi” in “(-pi/2,pi/2]”. The name identifies the same probe-specific toroidal angle; rad and magnetic_field_diagnostics are appropriate.

C.rationale: The source identifies the “Toroidal angle of the projection of a toroidal field (B_φ) probe's normal vector onto the horizontal plane,” with values “modulo pi” in “(-pi/2,pi/2].” The name and stored definition describe this same probe-orientation angle; radians and magnetic_field_diagnostics are appropriate.

A.rationale: The standard name, stored definition, and Data Dictionary sources all describe the lower bound or minimum threshold of photon energy for an energy band or detector channel/pixel.

B.rationale: The shared quantity is the lower photon-energy edge of an X-ray band: the sources call it the “Lower bound of the energy band” or the pixel threshold where “photons are counted only if their energy is above this value.” The documentation covers both “detection or emission band,” and eV is an energy unit.

C.rationale: The shared quantity is the lower photon-energy boundary of an X-ray energy window. Sources specify “Lower bound of the energy band” or “Lower energy detection threshold on each pixel”; the documentation covers “an X-ray detection or emission band,” distinguishing counting thresholds from emission-band boundaries.

A.rationale: normalized poloidal flux coordinate

B.rationale: Stored documentation: “The coordinate is the square-root form, ρ_pol,norm = √ψ_N.” Source 18 instead identifies “Normalised poloidal flux coordinate (ψ_norm)” and says “the flux being normalized” from axis to separatrix; that is the linear normalized flux ψ_N, not its square root.

C.rationale: Source 18 identifies “ψ_norm,” with “the flux being normalized to run from 0 at the magnetic axis to 1 at the separatrix.” The stored definition instead mandates “the square root of the poloidal-flux fraction.” Linear normalized poloidal flux and its square-root coordinate are different quantities.

A.rationale: The source, name, and stored definition all describe the loop voltage at the plasma boundary (last closed flux surface), with unit V representing the toroidal electromotive force driving ohmic current.

B.rationale: The sources describe “Loop voltage ... at the last closed flux surface (LCFS), the inductive EMF driving ohmic current”; the name and definition describe that same boundary loop voltage, with the appropriate unit V.

C.rationale: The source's “Loop voltage (Vloop) at the last closed flux surface (LCFS)” matches “loop_voltage_at_plasma_boundary” and the documented “closed toroidal loop at the plasma boundary”: the boundary toroidal electromotive force driving ohmic current, measured in V.

A.rationale: The source, standard name, and stored definition all describe the flux-surface average of the inverse square of the magnetic field magnitude, with consistent units of T^-2 and assigned domain equilibrium.

B.rationale: Source: “Flux surface averaged inverse square of the total magnetic field, ⟨1/B²⟩ (gm4), as a radial profile.” The name and definition identify that same average of B⁻² for the total equilibrium field magnitude; source and stored unit are both “T^-2”, and the enclosing equilibrium structure supports the assigned domain.

C.rationale: The source’s “Flux surface averaged inverse square of the total magnetic field, ⟨1/B²⟩” is the quantity identified by the name and defined as “Flux-surface average of the inverse square of total equilibrium magnetic-field magnitude.” T^-2 and the equilibrium domain are consistent.

A.rationale: The standard name, definition, and source text all consistently describe the flux-surface-averaged major radius \langle R \rangle in meters as an equilibrium profile metric coefficient.

B.rationale: The source states “Flux surface averaged major radius (gm8 = 〈R〉)” and “Represents the mean major radius over a flux surface”; the name and stored definition identify that same averaged radius, with the appropriate unit “m” and physics domain “equilibrium”.

C.rationale: The source states “Flux surface averaged major radius (gm8 = 〈R〉),” matching the name and stored definition, “Major radius averaged over a complete closed magnetic flux surface.” All identify the same quantity. The unit m and equilibrium domain are consistent.

A.rationale: The source specifies the locus as an "ICRH antenna module" within enclosing structure "ic_antennas/antenna/module" ("Set of antenna modules"), but the standard name omits the module locus, naming only the overall "ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna".

B.rationale: The source states “Phase of the forward power wave for an ICRH antenna module, measured relative to the first module,” and the enclosing locus is “Set of antenna modules.” The name only says “forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna,” omitting the module locus and the first-module relative-phase reference.

C.rationale: The source specifies “for an ICRH antenna module, measured relative to the first module.” Documentation confirms “one selected module relative to the first module.” The name identifies antenna-level forward-wave phase without the module locus or first-module reference, leaving out source qualifiers and differing from the stored definition’s module-relative scope.

A.rationale: The standard name and definition specify a limiter tile, but the source text establishes the component as a limiter unit (wall/description_2d/limiter/unit: 'Set of limiter units') representing the 'limiting surface', not a tile.

B.rationale: Source “Vertical (Z) coordinate of outline” with unit “m”, under “Irregular outline of the limiting surface” and “Set of limiter units”, matches the stored “Signed vertical (Z) coordinate of each point on a limiter-tile boundary contour”; structural_components fits this limiter geometry quantity.

C.rationale: The shared quantity is the vertical coordinate of the limiter outline: the source states “Vertical (Z) coordinate of outline” within an “Irregular outline of the limiting surface.” The stored definition likewise specifies the “Signed vertical (Z) coordinate of each point” on that contour. Metres and structural_components fit this geometric quantity.

A.rationale: The source, name, and definition describe the change in the vacuum toroidal magnetic field product with major radius, known as the vacuum poloidal current function, relative to its initial value at the start of plasma.

B.rationale: The source’s “Change in the vacuum toroidal field product … from the start of plasma” matches the stored “ΔF_vac=F_vac−F_vac,initial=R B_φ,vac−R B_φ,vac,initial”: one signed change in vacuum field times major radius. The unit T.m and domain magnetic_field_systems fit.

C.rationale: The source specifies “from the start of plasma” and “in the TF magnet system.” The name’s “initial_vacuum_poloidal_current_function” does not identify the plasma-start reference, and the name leaves the TF-magnet scope unstated.

rows.name: length_of_fiber_optic_current_sensor
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “Total length of the spun optical fibre wound on the vacuum vessel” and reiterates “Spun fibre length on the vacuum vessel.” The name “length_of_fiber_optic_current_sensor” omits the vacuum-vessel locus.

rows.name: length_variation_of_interferometer_beam
rows.C_rationale: The shared quantity is plasma-induced optical-path variation along an interferometer beam. The source states “Optical path length variation (ΔL) due to the plasma,” and the stored description specifies “optical-path difference relative to the corresponding no-plasma reference.”

rows.name: line_averaged_beryllium_density
rows.C_rationale: The source places “Beryllium” under “Ion density per species,” explicitly grouping “line-averaged ion density (ni) per ion species.” The name omits the ion basis. The stored definition confirms “beryllium ions” and explicitly excludes “neutral beryllium atoms.”

rows.name: line_averaged_electron_temperature
rows.C_rationale: The source states “Electron temperature (Te), line-averaged along a chord through the plasma,” matching the name and stored “Temperature of bulk electrons averaged along a specified plasma chord.” The unit eV is appropriate for electron temperature.

rows.name: line_averaged_tungsten_density
rows.C_rationale: The name “line_averaged_tungsten_density” leaves the tungsten counting scope unrestricted, whereas the definition specifies “tungsten ions” and “excluding neutral tungsten atoms.” The name is broader than the definition’s ion-only quantity.

rows.name: line_integrated_neutral_beam_radiance_at_spectral_line
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “radiances of the 9 Stark-split components,” and the stored definition specifies “Photon radiance of an individual motional-Stark component.” The name omits the individual Stark-component qualifier and instead describes the broader neutral-beam radiance at a spectral line.

rows.name: linear_growth_rate_normalized_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “for a given wavevector in the local flux-tube geometry,” and the definition requires “the local flux-tube approximation.” The name leaves out that local scope, encompassing global as well as local gyrokinetic eigenmodes.

rows.name: lithium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
rows.C_rationale: The enclosing source specifies “Gas injection rates in equivalent electrons.s^-1,” and the stored definition specifies “each injected lithium atom contributing three equivalent-electron counts.” The name “lithium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection” omits this equivalent-electron counting basis.

rows.name: lower_bound_energy_of_neutron_detector
rows.C_rationale: The name and live “neutron_lower_bound_energy_of_neutron_detector” both denote the source’s “Lower energy bound of a neutron detector energy band,” matching the stored definition’s “Lower kinetic-energy boundary of a neutron detector spectral band.”

rows.name: methane_carbon_13_prefill_count
rows.C_rationale: Source 1 states “Methane (CH4)” without isotope restriction, whereas the name specifies “carbon_13” and the definition “excludes methane containing other carbon isotopes.” The enclosing source specifies “prefill in equivalent electrons”; the name’s bare “count” omits this counting basis.

rows.name: minimum_gas_flow
rows.C_rationale: The shared quantity is minimum gas throughput: the source specifies the “lower operational bound on gas throughput,” and the definition specifies the “smallest pressure-volume gas throughput that a gas injection valve can reliably deliver.” Both source and stored units are “Pa.m^3.s^-1.”

rows.name: minor_angle_of_pellet_injector
rows.C_rationale: The name "minor_angle_of_pellet_injector" omits the shatter-cone scope. The source specifies the "minor opening angle of the elliptic fragment dispersion cone geometry"; the stored definition likewise specifies the "half-opening of the elliptic fragment-dispersion cone", not a general injector angle.

rows.name: minor_length_of_conductor_cross_section
rows.C_rationale: The source identifies the side by 'angle beta with respect to the height axis,' calling it 'one of the two oblique side dimensions.' Neither establishes a minor-side ordering. The name's 'minor_length' and definition's 'minor oblique dimension' instead identify a size-ranked dimension, which need not be the beta-defined side.

rows.name: molecular_fraction
rows.C_rationale: “Relative molecular fraction of a gas species within the injected gas mixture” is consistent with “molecular_fraction,” dimensionless unit “1,” and the fueling domain.

rows.name: motional_stark_radiance_of_spectral_line
rows.C_rationale: The name states “radiance,” whose unit is W·m^-2·sr^-1. The stored “m^-2.s^-1.sr^-1” instead fits photon-number radiance, lacking the energy factor required for unqualified radiance.

rows.name: neutral_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
rows.C_rationale: The stored definition states “Kinetic energy flux of neutral particles at the wall due to surface emission.” This requires energy per area per time, such as W.m^-2. The stored unit “m^-2.s^-1” lacks the energy dimension, even though the source repeats it.

rows.name: neutral_power_of_divertor
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “Net power deposited on the divertor targets” and “summed over all targets.” The name omits the net qualifier and target-only locus. Stored documentation instead includes “other divertor plasma-facing components,” expanding deposition beyond the source’s targets.

rows.name: neutron_energy
rows.C_rationale: Source 1 specifies 'discrete neutron energy values within a defined energy band'. The stored description instead specifies 'Kinetic energy per source neutron specifying a discrete energy-bin value for an energy-resolved neutron-detector response', restricting it to Source 2's response-grid role. This also makes the stored definition narrower than 'neutron_energy'.

rows.name: neutron_lower_bound_energy_of_neutron_detector
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies the “Lower energy bound of a neutron detector energy band.” The other live name, “lower_bound_energy_of_neutron_detector,” denotes the same boundary; the additional “neutron_” does not identify a distinct quantity.

rows.name: neutron_rate_of_neutron_detector
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies a “neutron detector channel operating in pulse counting mode,” within “Set of Measuring Modes simultaneously used by the detector.” The name “neutron_rate_of_neutron_detector” omits the pulse-counting-mode qualifier.

rows.name: normalized_effective_particle_energy
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “Normalised gradient (with respect to r_minor_norm) of the effective potential energy.” The name instead identifies normalized effective particle energy, and the definition specifies a “ratio of a species effective particle-energy coordinate to the positive species reference thermal-energy scale,” not a potential-energy gradient.

rows.name: normalized_perturbed_parallel_gyrocenter_energy_bessel_0
rows.C_rationale: The name’s “parallel_gyrocenter_energy” denotes parallel energy, but the source specifies “integral over 0.5·m·v_∥·v_⊥².” The stored definition likewise describes “coupling parallel motion to perpendicular kinetic energy.” This is a mixed parallel-velocity–perpendicular-energy moment, not a parallel-energy moment.

rows.name: normalized_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field_amplitude
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “normalised to the sum of amplitudes of all perturbed fields”; the name says only “normalized,” omitting that normalization basis. Stored documentation says the context “does not define its amplitude normalization,” contradicting the explicit source relation.

rows.name: normalized_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential_magnitude
rows.C_rationale: The name "normalized_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential_magnitude" identifies a scalar magnitude, but the documentation refers to a "declared vector-valued parent." The description also claims "the accepted standard name is empty," rather than defining the supplied quantity.

rows.name: normalized_perturbed_perpendicular_gyrocenter_energy_moment
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “weighted by 0.5·m·v⊥²·v²” and “in a linear eigenmode.” The name omits the mixed perpendicular-speed-squared × total-kinetic-energy weighting and the linear-eigenmode scope. The stored definition and integral agree with the source’s explicit kernel.

rows.name: normalized_plasma_internal_inductance
rows.C_rationale: The shared quantity is global, dimensionless normalized plasma internal inductance. The source specifies “li_3 = 2/R0/mu0^2/Ip^2 * int(Bp^2 dV),” matching the stored li(3) formula. The enclosing structure supplies global scope; unit “1” and the equilibrium domain are appropriate.

rows.name: normalized_toroidal_displacement_of_pellet_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
rows.C_rationale: The name states “normalized_toroidal_displacement_of_pellet,” but the source specifies “Radial drift of the pellet deposition location relative to the ablation location.” The definition specifies a “difference in normalized toroidal flux coordinate,” not toroidal displacement. The name omits the flux-coordinate convention and deposition-relative-to-ablation relation.

rows.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_plasma_boundary
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “at the separatrix radial position,” and the stored description says “at the magnetic separatrix.” The name instead specifies “at_plasma_boundary.” The stored documentation explicitly says the plasma-boundary and separatrix quantities “retain distinct locus semantics.”

rows.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_sawtooth_inversion_radius
rows.C_rationale: Source 1 specifies “at the sawtooth inversion radius,” matching the name. The stored description instead specifies the “unity-safety-factor rational surface,” and the documentation explicitly says these loci “need not coincide.” Thus the stored definition changes Source 1’s locus and disagrees with the name.

rows.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_of_reflectometer_cutoff_position
rows.C_rationale: The name specifies “reflectometer_cutoff_position”, but the source specifies “Doppler reflectometer measurement position” and the stored description says “Doppler reflectometer measurement location”. The name substitutes a cutoff-specific locus for the stated measurement locus and omits the explicit Doppler specialization.

rows.name: normalized_toroidal_hard_xray_peak_lower_bound_width
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies an “Internal (towards magnetic axis) half-width” in “normalised toroidal flux coordinate,” matching the stored “Lower-side half-width” in that coordinate. This is the same quantity as the live name “inner_hard_xray_half_width_at_emissivity_peak.”

rows.name: nuclear_power_density_of_breeder_blanket_layer
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “evaluated at the outboard midplane,” a locus absent from the name. The stored documentation instead describes a layer-wide spatial field whose “volume integral gives the corresponding layer-integrated nuclear heating power,” rather than the source’s midplane-only quantity.

rows.name: outer_hard_xray_half_width_at_emissivity_peak
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “in normalised toroidal flux coordinate (ρtor,norm),” and the enclosing structure specifies “Emissivity profile per energy band.” The name omits both the coordinate convention and the per-energy-band basis.

rows.name: oxygen_count_accumulated_due_to_gas_injection
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies accumulation “since the plasma breakdown” and “in equivalent electrons”; neither qualifier appears in the name. The definition specifies “eight count units per neutral oxygen atom,” an equivalent-electron count rather than the oxygen count stated by the name.

rows.name: oxygen_density_at_divertor_target
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “Ion density (ni) per individual ion species,” and the definition specifies “oxygen ions” while “excluding neutral oxygen.” The name “oxygen_density_at_divertor_target” omits this ion-only population restriction and therefore has broader scope than the stored definition.

rows.name: oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “Oxygen” within “Ion density (ni) per species at the separatrix.” This matches oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary and the stored “Number density of oxygen ions at the plasma boundary,” evaluated on the “last closed magnetic flux surface.” The unit m^-3 fits this number density.

rows.name: parallel_per_toroidal_mode_wave_phase
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “Phase of the parallel component of the wave electric field,” and the stored definition calls it “the local angular argument.” The stored unit “V.m^-1” measures electric-field strength, not angular phase, which requires radians or a dimensionless unit.

rows.name: parallel_wave_electric_field_imaginary_part
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “Imaginary part of the parallel electric field component (E∥),” and its enclosing structure states “Parallel to magnetic field.” The name and stored definition identify this same magnetic-field-aligned imaginary wave-electric-field component. The stored unit V.m^-1 matches the source and quantity.

rows.name: pellet_angle_at_shattering_position
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies an “Impact (grazing) angle” that is “the complement of the incidence angle.” The name “pellet_angle_at_shattering_position” omits the grazing-angle reference convention, leaving it indistinguishable from a normal-referenced incidence angle.

rows.name: per_toroidal_mode_fast_electron_power_density
rows.C_rationale: The shared quantity is fast-electron absorbed power per unit volume, resolved by toroidal mode: “Absorbed wave power density on the fast electron population, decomposed per toroidal mode number n_phi.” The stored definition accommodates both the poloidal-cross-section and flux-surface-averaged representations; W.m^-3 and auxiliary_heating are appropriate.

rows.name: per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power
rows.C_rationale: The name’s 'fast_ion' and definition’s 'fast ions' conflict with Source 1 documentation’s 'thermal species'. Source 1 specifies 'inside a flux surface', omitted from the name. The definition restricts power to a 'selected magnetic flux surface', unlike the name’s unqualified power scope and Source 2’s 'global_quantities' scope.

rows.name: per_toroidal_mode_flux_surface_averaged_parallel_wave_electric_field_amplitude
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “E∥/n_phi” and “power-deposition-density weighting.” The name identifies a mode-resolved field amplitude rather than the stated mode-number-normalized quantity and omits deposition weighting. The documentation explicitly contradicts the normalization: “no summation over modes or division by mode number is implied.”

rows.name: per_toroidal_mode_total_absorbed_wave_power
rows.C_rationale: Source 1 specifies power “enclosed within a flux surface,” a locus omitted from the name. Stored documentation instead says “integrated over the full plasma volume” and “not restricted to a species, population, or selected flux-surface region.” This contradicts Source 1, although it matches Source 2’s global scope.

rows.name: per_toroidal_mode_total_absorbed_wave_power_density
rows.C_rationale: The shared quantity is absorbed wave power density per toroidal mode. Source: “Absorbed wave power density per toroidal mode number”; definition: “Volumetric rate of coherent-wave energy deposition into all plasma particle populations for each toroidal Fourier mode.” W.m^-3 and the waves domain are consistent.

rows.name: per_toroidal_mode_wave_phase
rows.C_rationale: The name states “wave_phase,” and the definition calls it the “local angular argument of a complex electric-field coefficient.” The stored unit “V.m^-1” measures electric-field strength, not angular phase; the documentation explicitly states that angular phase “is dimensionless.”

rows.name: perpendicular_gyrocenter_heat_perturbed_flux_normalized_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode
rows.C_rationale: The source’s “0.5·m·v_parallel·v_perp²” describes parallel transport of perpendicular kinetic energy, explicitly a “mixed parallel-perpendicular energy-weighted moment.” The name’s “perpendicular_gyrocenter_heat_perturbed_flux” and stored definition’s “perpendicular heat flux moment” instead identify the flux itself as perpendicular.

rows.name: perpendicular_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_pressure
rows.C_rationale: Source documentation says “Normalised perpendicular temperature,” contradicting both the name’s “pressure” and the stored definition’s “perpendicular gyrotropic pressure moment.” The source is internally inconsistent: its description instead says “Normalised perpendicular pressure,” which agrees with the stored name and definition.

rows.name: perturbed_electrostatic_potential_amplitude
rows.C_rationale: The definition states “the modulus of the perturbation” for an electrostatic potential, and documentation distinguishes a “normalized” reference-scaled quantity. The named, unnormalized potential amplitude has units of volts, not the stored unit “1”.

rows.name: poloidal_cumulative_lost_magnetic_flux_due_to_resistive_dissipation
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies a “time-integrated volume-averaged product of toroidal electric field and ohmic current density normalised by the plasma current.” The name omits the stated volume averaging and plasma-current normalization.

rows.name: poloidal_electron_beta_flux_surface_averaged_at_pedestal_top
rows.C_rationale: Source 1 specifies “using the low field side magnetic poloidal field.” The name instead states “flux_surface_averaged,” and the documentation specifies “the square of the averaged field magnitude,” explicitly distinguishing local-field quantities. Sources 2–3 support the averaged quantity but do not remove the contradiction with Source 1.

rows.name: poloidal_neutral_state_momentum_source
rows.C_rationale: The enclosing source specifies a “neutral species charge state” and “different charge states.” The name’s “neutral_state” omits that charge-state basis. The stored definition instead specifies “one specified internal state,” and the documentation excludes contributions from other internal states, substituting internal-state resolution for charge-state resolution.

rows.name: power_of_plant_subsystem
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “Electrical power consumed by an individual subsystem.” Stored documentation likewise specifies “real electrical power consumed” and “excludes thermal power and electrical generation.” The name “power_of_plant_subsystem” omits the electrical-consumption restriction and is broader than the stored definition.

rows.name: pressure_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “Gas pressure inside the vacuum tank of a lower hybrid (LH) antenna.” The name omits the gas qualifier and vacuum-tank locus. The stored definition includes “mechanical contact pressure acting on antenna surfaces or structures,” broadening the quantity beyond the source’s gas pressure.

rows.name: radial_coordinate_of_detector_pixel
rows.C_rationale: The shared quantity is the major-radius coordinate of each detector-pixel centre. Source “Major radius (R) coordinate of pixel position” and enclosing “Position of the centre of each pixel” agree with the stored “Major-radius coordinate of the detector pixel” in the cylindrical frame.

rows.name: radial_coordinate_of_pellet_path
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “Major radius (R) coordinate of position” within “Position along the pellet path.” The listed live name “radial_coordinate_of_pellet_path_point” denotes that same coordinate, so the two names duplicate one quantity.

rows.name: radial_coordinate_of_pellet_path_point
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “Major radius (R) coordinate of position” within “Position along the pellet path.” The live name “radial_coordinate_of_pellet_path” denotes this same quantity; adding “point” does not distinguish another quantity.

rows.name: radial_coordinate_of_poloidal_field_coil
rows.C_rationale: The shared quantity is the “Major radius (R) coordinate” of a specified point in the “Cross-sectional shape of the coil.” The stored definition identifies this as the “Major-radius coordinate of a reference point in a poloidal-field coil's cross-sectional geometry.” Metres and magnetic_field_systems are appropriate.

rows.name: radial_coordinate_of_reflector
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “Major radius (R) coordinate of sphere centre” and “in the case of a spherical mirror.” The name omits that locus and geometry restriction. The stored definition likewise specifies a “spherical reflector's sphere center,” a narrower scope than the name’s unqualified reflector radial coordinate.

rows.name: radial_distance_at_midplane
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “from the first wall,” “zero defined at the first wall surface,” and “of a breeding blanket module.” The name states only “radial_distance_at_midplane,” omitting the wall-referenced coordinate origin and the blanket-module locus.

rows.name: radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential
rows.C_rationale: The stored definition identifies a “perturbed magnetic vector-potential eigenfunction in the vacuum region for a toroidal linear-MHD mode.” This is a linear-MHD quantity, not a gyrokinetic quantity as the assigned domain “gyrokinetics” states.

rows.name: radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential_imaginary_part
rows.C_rationale: The assigned domain is "gyrokinetics", but the source describes the quantity as "from linear MHD stability analysis" and places it under "MHD modes in the vacuum".

rows.name: radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential_real_part
rows.C_rationale: The assigned domain is “gyrokinetics,” but the source describes an eigenfunction “from linear MHD stability analysis for a given toroidal mode number,” enclosed by “MHD modes in the vacuum.” The source quantity belongs to linear MHD stability, not gyrokinetics.

rows.name: radial_separatrix_distance_at_outboard_midplane
rows.C_rationale: The shared quantity is the signed radial separation from the separatrix at the outboard midplane, in metres: “mapped along flux surfaces to the outboard midplane, in the major radius direction.” The source’s “Positive value means the measurement is outside of the separatrix” agrees with the stored definition.

rows.name: radial_width_of_active_spatial_resolution_zone
rows.C_rationale: The definition restricts the quantity to “a visible spectrometer channel,” but Source 1 describes “MSE diagnostic measurement channels (lines of sight).” That restriction excludes one supplied source scope and disagrees with the broader name, “radial_width_of_active_spatial_resolution_zone.”

rows.name: radius_of_bragg_crystal
rows.C_rationale: The shared quantity is the Bragg crystal’s circular-aperture radius. The source specifies “Radius of a circular X-ray crystal aperture” defining the crystal’s physical size; the stored definition likewise says “physical extent, not surface curvature.”

rows.name: radius_of_poloidal_field_coil
rows.C_rationale: The name 'radius_of_poloidal_field_coil' identifies a coil radius, but the definition specifies the 'curvature radius of one arc-of-circle segment used to approximate the cross-sectional contour'—the local radius of a contour segment, not the radius of the coil.

rows.name: ratio_of_ion_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_ion_temperature
rows.C_rationale: Source specifies “averaged over ion species and states” and “plasma volume up to the LCFS”; the name omits these qualifiers. Stored documentation instead says “Both operands refer to the same specified ion species,” contradicting the source’s average over species.

rows.name: ratio_of_nuclear_energy_to_incident_neutron_energy
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies an “Energy multiplication factor (M) of the breeding blanket,” and the stored definition likewise locates both energies in that blanket. The name “ratio_of_nuclear_energy_to_incident_neutron_energy” omits the breeding-blanket locus.

rows.name: ratio_of_particle_temperature_to_particle_reference_temperature
rows.C_rationale: The source’s “Normalised temperature (T/T_ref) of a particle species” matches the named temperature ratio and the definition’s “Dimensionless ratio comparing a particle species’ kinetic temperature with the positive reference temperature on the same magnetic flux surface.” Unit “1” is appropriate.

rows.name: resistivity_of_plasma_facing_component
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “Electrical resistivity of a mobile plasma-facing component (PFC) unit,” and the stored definition specifies “a mobile plasma-facing component unit.” The name “resistivity_of_plasma_facing_component” omits the mobile-unit qualifier and therefore describes a broader scope than the source and stored definition.

rows.name: right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “One scalar value” per grid element; documentation instead defines a “vector contribution.” The source also says this component “drives ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH),” whereas documentation says it “rotates opposite to positive-ion gyromotion” and assigns ion co-rotation to the complementary left-hand component.

rows.name: right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_real_part
rows.C_rationale: The source’s “Real part of the right-hand circularly polarized electric field component (E−)” matches the name’s “electric_field_real_part” and the definition’s “Signed in-phase quadrature of the right-hand circular E-minus wave electric-field phasor.” All identify the same electric-field quadrature, correctly measured in V.m^-1.

rows.name: safety_factor_at_pedestal_top
rows.C_rationale: The source's “Safety factor” is enclosed by “Parameters at pedestal top.” The other live name “safety_factor_at_pedestal,” produced by the same source, denotes this same pedestal-top safety factor.

rows.name: second_local_tangential_width_of_diagnostic_aperture
rows.C_rationale: The definition specifies a “neutron detector collimating aperture,” but the sources describe a “visible camera aperture” and reflectometer antenna apertures. The name’s generic “diagnostic_aperture” also differs in scope from the definition’s neutron-detector-only quantity.

rows.name: shattered_pellet_species_number_density_of_pellet
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “within the shell layer,” but the name says “of_pellet,” omitting the shell-only locus. The stored documentation explicitly limits the density to “only to the shell material, excluding the pellet core and surrounding gas” and says it “is not averaged over the entire pellet.”

rows.name: spectral_efficiency_of_filter
rows.C_rationale: The shared quantity is the filter’s wavelength-dependent photon-detection efficiency. The source states “Detection efficiency of the visible bremsstrahlung diagnostic filter as a function of photon wavelength” and “Probability of detection of a photon impacting the detector”; the stored definition likewise specifies the probability that the photon “is registered as a detection event.”

rows.name: speed_at_shattering_position
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies the “SPI pellet centre of mass immediately before shattering.” The name “speed_at_shattering_position” identifies only a speed and location, omitting the pellet centre-of-mass basis and the immediately-before-shattering timing.

rows.name: square_of_ion_state_charge_number
rows.C_rationale: Source says “Average Z square of the charge state bundle” with “relative concentration”; definition says “Concentration-weighted mean”. The name instead specifies a state's squared charge number, omitting bundle averaging and weighting. Charge-number squared is dimensionless, not “e”. Source scope includes “Edge plasma quantities”, inconsistent with the core-only domain assignment.

rows.name: stray_breakdown_magnetic_field_magnitude
rows.C_rationale: The name and stored “Magnitude of the residual magnetic field at the plasma position during initiation” identify the scalar strength of the source’s “Stray magnetic field (Bstray) at the plasma position during plasma initiation.” The unit “T” fits magnetic-field magnitude.

rows.name: thermal_power_of_breeder_blanket
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “Thermal power directed toward the tritium breeding blanket module.” The name omits the module locus and incoming direction. Stored documentation instead says “aggregates heat deposition at the blanket level,” changing module-scoped heat input into blanket-wide aggregation.

rows.name: thickness_of_breeder_blanket_layer
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “Thickness of a breeding blanket module layer evaluated at the midplane” and “Thickness of this layer evaluated at the midplane.” The name “thickness_of_breeder_blanket_layer” omits the midplane locus.

rows.name: thickness_of_cryostat
rows.C_rationale: Sources specify 'cryostat thermal shield', thickness 'evaluated at the midplane', and annular-layer thickness in the 'perpendicular direction to the centreline'. The name omits these component, locus and measurement qualifiers. The definition instead specifies the 'cryostat structural vessel' and 'local wall-normal direction', conflicting with the thermal-shield scope and centreline-based measurement.

rows.name: tilt_angle_of_coil_conductor_element
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “Inclination angle beta (β) of the second oblique side” in the “trapezoidal cross-section” of an “active PF coil element.” The stored definition agrees. “tilt_angle_of_coil_conductor_element” omits these qualifiers and describes a broader scope than the particular side inclination defined.

rows.name: toroidal_angle_of_detector
rows.C_rationale: “toroidal_angle_of_detector” identifies the detector’s angle, but the source specifies “Toroidal angle (φ) coordinate of emission grid,” enclosing “neutron emission cells in the plasma.” The stored documentation instead specifies “individual plasma emission positions, not to the detector's own location, viewing direction, or angular acceptance.”

rows.name: toroidal_angle_of_measurement_position
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “R, Z, Phi position of the NBI unit centre,” contradicting the measurement locus asserted by the name and definition (“Toroidal angle of the measurement position”). These sources describe geometrical coordinates of hardware and diagnostic locations across systems, rather than equilibrium quantities; the assigned “equilibrium” domain is inappropriate.

rows.name: toroidal_angular_width_of_limiter_tile
rows.C_rationale: Source describes “extensions of a limiter unit” as a “list of zones defined by their centre and full width,” with multiple “toroidal occurrences.” The name’s “limiter_tile” and definition’s “Full toroidal angular span of one limiter tile” instead identify a complete individual tile’s span, not a limiter-unit zone’s width.

rows.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_reciprocating_probe
rows.C_rationale: The source specifies “Toroidal angle (φ) coordinate of position average,” enclosed by “Average position of the measurements derived from multiple collectors” under “plunge.” The name omits this averaging and per-plunge scope, while the stored definition explicitly identifies the “average measurement position during a plunge.”

rows.name: toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude
rows.C_rationale: The name and definition identify the local toroidal-flux-coordinate gradient magnitude: “the magnitude of its spatial gradient,” explicitly “not intrinsically flux-surface averaged or squared.” Unit 1 is compatible with a length-valued toroidal-flux coordinate; no recorded source establishes a conflicting coordinate convention.

rows.name: toroidal_total_plasma_volumetric_angular_momentum
rows.C_rationale: Source 1’s enclosing structure specifies “SOL radial profiles ... taken on outboard equatorial mid-plane.” The name omits this evaluation locus, and the stored documentation contradicts it by stating “No particular evaluation locus is imposed.”

rows.name: total_absorbed_wave_power_at_inside_flux_surface
rows.C_rationale: The name, definition, and source identify total absorbed wave power inside a flux surface. rows.name: total_absorbed_wave_power_density

prompts.system:
You are an independent physics auditor of the standard names of a fusion data dictionary. A standard name identifies exactly one quantity. You are given one name record at a time and must decide which of these fixed defect classes apply to it:

- `name_contradicts_source`: The name states a quantity, locus, component or relation that the Data Dictionary source text contradicts.
- `name_omits_source`: The source text states a qualifier of the quantity — a counting basis, a species basis, a weighting or average, a normalisation, a coordinate convention, a component or a locus — and the name leaves it out.
- `definition_contradicts_source`: The stored definition (description or documentation) contradicts the Data Dictionary source text.
- `name_definition_disagree`: The stored name and the stored definition describe different quantities or different scopes, even if each is internally consistent.
- `unit_wrong`: The stored unit does not fit the quantity the name states: it is dimensionally wrong for that kind of quantity, or it is the wrong unit for the stated kind of quantity.
- `wrong_physics_domain`: The assigned physics domain is not the domain of the quantity the source describes.
- `duplicate_of_live_name`: The name denotes the same quantity as another live standard name listed for it, so the catalog carries one quantity twice.

Rules:
- Report every class that applies. A name may carry more than one.
- Report an empty list when no class applies. Do not invent a defect, and do not flag a name for style, brevity, missing prose, or for information no part of the record states.
- A qualifier stated by a source's enclosing structure is stated by the source. Report a missing qualifier only when neither the source leaf nor any enclosing structure states it.
- Report a duplicate only against a name in the list of other live names given for the record.
- If the record carries no Data Dictionary text, judge only the classes that need no source: name_definition_disagree, unit_wrong, wrong_physics_domain, duplicate_of_live_name.
- Quote the stored or source wording that decides the verdict. At most 60 words.
- Return the JSON object the schema asks for; no other text.
